lessons.title: Bonjour, mes amis!
lessons.oneGoal: Students will recognize and respond to basic French greetings through gestures and visual cues

opening.activity: Gentle introduction with puppet saying 'Bonjour!' and waving. Show friendly face pictures of children greeting each other.
opening.visualSupports: Big wave gesture for 'bonjour', hand to heart for 'merci', wave goodbye for 'au revoir'

main.activity: Circle time with greeting song using gestures. Pass the puppet around for each child to hear 'Bonjour [name]!' Practice greeting responses with thumbs up, wave, or smile.
main.visualSupports: Exaggerated facial expressions, large gesture demonstrations, picture sequence cards showing greeting interactions

decisionPoints.question: How comfortable are students with new sounds?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Continue with puppet conversations and encourage verbal responses
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on gestures and visual responses, extend listening time

decisionPoints.question: What level of gestures/TPR support is needed?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Use full body movements and exaggerated gestures
decisionPoints.ifNo: Use simple hand gestures and facial expressions

closing.activity: Goodbye circle with puppet saying 'Au revoir!' to each child. Practice waving and saying goodbye.

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students seem overwhelmed by new sounds
troubleshooting.then: Use more gestures, slower pace, and focus on just 'bonjour' with lots of repetition

lessons.realWorldConnection: How people greet each other in French-speaking communities around the world

lessons.title: Je m'appelle...
lessons.oneGoal: Students will understand name introductions and begin to share their names using gestures and visual supports

opening.activity: Review 'Bonjour!' from Lesson 1 with puppet. Puppet introduces itself: 'Je m'appelle Pierre!'
opening.visualSupports: Point to self gesture for 'je', point to name tag for 'm'appelle', questioning gesture for 'comment'

main.activity: Name introduction circle. Puppet asks 'Comment tu t'appelles?' to each child. Use name cards with photos. Practice pointing to self and saying/showing names.
main.visualSupports: Point to self clearly, hold up name cards, use questioning facial expressions and hand gestures

decisionPoints.question: Are students ready to say their names or still observing?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Encourage verbal attempts with puppet support
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on pointing to name cards and self-recognition activities

decisionPoints.question: How much repetition is needed for name patterns?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Repeat pattern with multiple examples and slow pace
decisionPoints.ifNo: Move to interactive name games and recognition activities

closing.activity: Goodbye circle where puppet says 'Au revoir [name]!' to each child while they hold their name card.

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students confused about name introduction pattern
troubleshooting.then: Use more visual name cards, practice with puppet first, focus on gestures before words

lessons.realWorldConnection: How introductions work in French families and communities

lessons.title: Les couleurs magiques
lessons.oneGoal: Students will recognize and respond to basic color words through visual objects and movement

opening.activity: Review greetings and names. Introduce color magic with colored scarves or fabric appearing from a box.
opening.visualSupports: Hold up colors clearly, use magic gestures, exaggerated surprise expressions

main.activity: Color exploration stations: touch red objects, find blue items, dance with yellow scarves. Color matching games with large visual cards.
main.visualSupports: Point clearly to colors, use searching gestures for finding activities, dancing movements for each color

decisionPoints.question: Which colors are students naturally drawn to?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Start with preferred colors and build confidence
decisionPoints.ifNo: Introduce all three colors equally with multiple exposures

decisionPoints.question: Should we use more movement games or quiet observation?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Focus on active color games and dancing with scarves
decisionPoints.ifNo: Use seated color sorting and matching activities

closing.activity: Color goodbye game: each child chooses a colored scarf and waves 'Au revoir rouge!' or their chosen color.

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students having difficulty distinguishing color words
troubleshooting.then: Use more physical objects, slower repetition, focus on one color at a time with multiple examples

lessons.realWorldConnection: Describing the colorful world around us - flowers, toys, clothes

lessons.title: Mes premiers nombres
lessons.oneGoal: Students will recognize numbers 1-5 through finger counting, songs, and visual representations

opening.activity: Review colors with finger painting gesture. Introduce counting with Pierre puppet showing fingers for 'un, deux, trois'.
opening.visualSupports: Clear finger counting gestures, large number visuals, rhythmic counting movements

main.activity: Counting song with finger actions. Count colored objects from previous lesson. Number hop: hop once for 'un', twice for 'deux', three times for 'trois'.
main.visualSupports: Exaggerated finger counting, clear pointing to numbers, hopping movements with counting rhythm

decisionPoints.question: How are students responding to finger counting?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Extend to more complex counting games and activities
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on simple finger recognition and one-to-one correspondence

decisionPoints.question: Should we focus on listening or include some speaking?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Encourage counting attempts with finger support
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on recognition and finger counting responses

closing.activity: Counting goodbye: count three waves 'un, deux, trois' and say 'Au revoir!' Pierre puppet counts students.

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students struggling with number-finger coordination
troubleshooting.then: Use larger visual number cards, practice finger counting slowly, focus on one number at a time

lessons.realWorldConnection: Counting everyday things - toys, books, fingers, age

lessons.title: Ma famille française
lessons.oneGoal: Students will understand family words through photos, drawings, and inclusive family representations

opening.activity: Review counting fingers and colors. Pierre puppet shows family photos and introduces 'Ma famille!'
opening.visualSupports: Heart gesture for 'famille', pointing to family members, warm facial expressions

main.activity: Family photo sharing circle. Students can share photos or draw their families. Practice 'maman', 'papa', 'famille' with inclusive examples (two moms, single parent, grandparents, etc.).
main.visualSupports: Hugging gesture for family love, pointing to family members, inclusive visual examples

decisionPoints.question: How do we honor diverse family structures?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Use inclusive examples and let children define their own families
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on traditional examples but remain open to student sharing

decisionPoints.question: Are students ready to share about their families?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Encourage sharing with puppet support and visual aids
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on listening and observing family examples

closing.activity: Family love circle: send hugs to our families and say 'Au revoir, famille!' with heart gestures.

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students emotional about family separation or differences
troubleshooting.then: Focus on love and connection, use puppet for comfort, validate all family structures

lessons.realWorldConnection: How French-speaking families talk about themselves and show love

lessons.title: Les animaux amusants
lessons.oneGoal: Students will recognize animal names through sounds, movements, and visual supports

opening.activity: Review family words with Pierre puppet. Introduce animal friends: puppet meets a 'chat' with meowing and paw gestures.
materials: animal puppets or toys (cat, dog, bird)
opening.visualSupports: Cat paw gestures, dog panting and tail wagging movements, bird flying motions

main.activity: Animal movement game: crawl like 'chat', pant like 'chien', fly like 'oiseau'. Animal sound matching and movement imitation with visual cards.
main.visualSupports: Clear animal movements, animal sound mimicking, pointing to animal features

decisionPoints.question: Which animal movements engage students most?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Focus on preferred animals and extend movement activities
decisionPoints.ifNo: Try different animals or use more visual/auditory approaches

decisionPoints.question: Should we include animal sounds or focus on names?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Combine sounds with names for multi-sensory learning
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on visual recognition and movement only

closing.activity: Animal goodbye parade: each child chooses an animal movement and sound to say goodbye.

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students overwhelmed by animal movements or sounds
troubleshooting.then: Use quieter activities, focus on gentle animal gestures, use stuffed animals for comfort

lessons.realWorldConnection: Animals in our neighborhoods, farms, and French-speaking countries

lessons.title: Mes parties du corps
lessons.oneGoal: Students will identify basic body parts through songs, movements, and touching exercises

opening.activity: Review animal movements using our bodies. Pierre puppet touches his 'tête' and asks students to touch theirs.
opening.visualSupports: Clear touching gestures, pointing to body parts, exaggerated movements

main.activity: Body part song with actions: 'Tête, épaules, genoux et pieds' adapted for 'tête, main, pied'. Simon Says game with body parts. Mirror exploration touching named parts.
main.visualSupports: Touch head for 'tête', wave hands for 'main', stomp feet for 'pied', mirror reflection activities

decisionPoints.question: How comfortable are students with body part songs?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Extend to more complex body part games and sequences
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on simple touching and pointing activities

decisionPoints.question: Should we use mirrors or partner activities?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Use mirrors for self-discovery and awareness
decisionPoints.ifNo: Use partner activities for social interaction

closing.activity: Body part goodbye: touch 'tête', wave 'main', stomp 'pied' and say 'Au revoir!'

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students uncomfortable with body part touching or movements
troubleshooting.then: Use puppet demonstrations, gentle pointing instead of touching, respect personal space

lessons.realWorldConnection: Taking care of our bodies and describing ourselves to others

lessons.title: Les objets de classe
lessons.oneGoal: Students will recognize classroom objects through touch, pointing, and simple commands

opening.activity: Review body parts by using them to find classroom objects. Pierre puppet picks up a 'crayon' with his 'main'.
opening.visualSupports: Clear pointing to objects, holding and touching gestures, searching movements

main.activity: Classroom scavenger hunt: find and touch 'crayon', 'livre', 'table'. Object sorting game. Practice giving and receiving classroom objects with simple commands.
main.visualSupports: Point clearly to objects, demonstrate searching, show giving and receiving gestures

decisionPoints.question: Which classroom objects are most meaningful to students?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Focus on familiar, frequently used objects
decisionPoints.ifNo: Introduce variety and let students explore preferences

decisionPoints.question: Should we use scavenger hunts or direct instruction?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Use active searching and discovery activities
decisionPoints.ifNo: Use seated demonstration and object manipulation

closing.activity: Object appreciation circle: each child holds a classroom object and we say 'Merci, crayon!' or 'Au revoir, livre!'

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students confused by similar-looking objects or commands
troubleshooting.then: Use more distinct objects, clearer visual differences, simpler one-step instructions

lessons.realWorldConnection: Using French to navigate and organize our learning space

lessons.title: J'aime et je n'aime pas
lessons.oneGoal: Students will express simple preferences through gestures, facial expressions, and visual supports

opening.activity: Review classroom objects. Pierre puppet shows strong love for a 'livre' saying 'J'aime!' with heart gesture.
materials: variety of objects from previous lessons
opening.visualSupports: Heart gesture for 'j'aime', X or shaking head for 'non', thumbs up for 'oui'

main.activity: Preference exploration: show objects/pictures and let students show thumbs up/down. Practice 'J'aime' with heart gesture and 'Non' with gentle head shake. Choice-making activities.
main.visualSupports: Exaggerated facial expressions, clear thumbs up/down gestures, heart hugging for likes

decisionPoints.question: How are students showing preferences non-verbally?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Build on their natural expressions and gestures
decisionPoints.ifNo: Model clear preference expressions and give time to practice

decisionPoints.question: Should we focus on positive expressions first?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Emphasize 'j'aime' and positive choices initially
decisionPoints.ifNo: Show both positive and negative equally

closing.activity: Preference sharing circle: each child shows one thing they love with 'J'aime' gesture and heart.

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students reluctant to express dislikes or make choices
troubleshooting.then: Focus on positive preferences first, use puppet to model, make choices less personal

lessons.realWorldConnection: Expressing what we like and don't like about food, activities, and things around us

lessons.title: Les actions quotidiennes
lessons.oneGoal: Students will understand basic action words through demonstration, mime, and physical response

opening.activity: Review preferences with movement: 'J'aime marcher!' Pierre puppet demonstrates walking, jumping, dancing.
opening.visualSupports: Clear walking steps, jumping movements, dancing gestures with rhythm

main.activity: Action station rotation: practice 'marcher' around the room, 'sauter' on mats, 'danser' to music. Action Simon Says game. Mime and guess activities.
main.visualSupports: Demonstrate each action clearly, use music and rhythm, encourage creative interpretation

decisionPoints.question: Which actions naturally engage student energy levels?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Focus on preferred actions and extend practice time
decisionPoints.ifNo: Try gentler versions or seated adaptations of actions

decisionPoints.question: Should we use more demonstration or student participation?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Encourage active student participation and leadership
decisionPoints.ifNo: Use more teacher/puppet demonstration with gradual participation

closing.activity: Action goodbye sequence: everyone 'marche' to the door, 'saute' twice, 'danse' and says 'Au revoir!'

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students too excited or overwhelmed by movement activities
troubleshooting.then: Use calmer versions, seated movements, or take movement breaks between actions

lessons.realWorldConnection: Describing what we do every day at home and school

lessons.title: Les saisons et météo
lessons.oneGoal: Students will recognize weather and season words through window observations, clothing, and sensory experiences

opening.activity: Review actions by 'marcher' to the window. Pierre puppet looks outside and comments on 'soleil' or 'pluie'.
opening.visualSupports: Point to sun/rain outside, sun gesture (arms up in circle), rain gesture (fingers falling down)

main.activity: Weather observation at window. Dress-up activity with seasonal clothes. Weather dance: sun dance, rain dance. Create weather chart for classroom.
main.visualSupports: Look outside together, demonstrate weather gestures, show seasonal clothing clearly

decisionPoints.question: How does current weather connect to lesson content?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Use actual weather as primary teaching tool
decisionPoints.ifNo: Use props and imagination to explore different weather

decisionPoints.question: Should we go outside or use window observations?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Take brief outdoor weather exploration if safe
decisionPoints.ifNo: Use window observations and weather simulation activities

closing.activity: Weather goodbye: check the weather, do appropriate weather gesture, and say goodbye to the sun or rain.

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students distracted by outdoor observations or weather anxiety
troubleshooting.then: Use calming weather discussions, focus on indoor comfort, use gentle weather imagery

lessons.realWorldConnection: Talking about weather and seasons affects our daily choices and activities

lessons.title: Mes émotions en français
lessons.oneGoal: Students will identify basic emotion words through facial expressions, body language, and scenarios

opening.activity: Review weather and connect to feelings: 'Soleil - heureux!' Pierre puppet shows big smile and happy dance.
opening.visualSupports: Exaggerated happy face for 'heureux', sad face for 'triste', yawning for 'fatigué'

main.activity: Emotion mirror exploration: practice faces in mirror. Emotion charades with puppet. Connect emotions to weather, colors, activities from previous lessons.
main.visualSupports: Model clear facial expressions, use whole body to show emotions, connect to familiar situations

decisionPoints.question: How are students expressing emotions non-verbally?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Build on natural expressions and validate feelings
decisionPoints.ifNo: Use puppet to model emotions safely and gradually

decisionPoints.question: Should we use mirrors, photos, or dramatic play?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Use approach that feels safest and most engaging for students
decisionPoints.ifNo: Try multiple approaches to find what works best

closing.activity: Emotion check-in circle: each child shows how they feel and we validate with 'Tu es heureux!' or appropriate emotion.

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students becoming emotional or upset during emotion exploration
troubleshooting.then: Focus on happy emotions, use puppet for safety, provide comfort and validation

lessons.realWorldConnection: Understanding and expressing how we feel in different situations

lessons.title: Notre routine française
lessons.oneGoal: Students will understand daily routine vocabulary through sequencing, clocks, and role-play activities

opening.activity: Review emotions during different times. Pierre puppet shows 'heureux' in 'matin' with sunrise picture.
opening.visualSupports: Point to sun for 'matin', high sun for 'midi', moon for 'soir'

main.activity: Daily routine picture sequencing: arrange morning, noon, evening activities. Role-play daily activities from previous lessons during different times. Create class routine chart.
main.visualSupports: Clear time gestures, sequence activities visually, connect to familiar daily experiences

decisionPoints.question: How do student daily routines connect to lesson content?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Use their actual routines as examples and practice
decisionPoints.ifNo: Create simple, universal routine examples

decisionPoints.question: Should we use picture schedules or physical demonstrations?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Use approach that best matches student learning styles
decisionPoints.ifNo: Combine both for comprehensive understanding

closing.activity: Time of day goodbye: identify current time of day and do appropriate goodbye for 'matin', 'midi', or 'soir'.

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students confused by time concepts or routine sequencing
troubleshooting.then: Use simpler sequences, focus on current time only, use very familiar activities

lessons.realWorldConnection: How French-speaking children structure their days and talk about time

lessons.title: Ma petite présentation
lessons.oneGoal: Students will demonstrate understanding through simple presentation combining all learned vocabulary and concepts

opening.activity: Review learning journey with picture cards from all lessons. Pierre puppet says he wants to 'présenter' his friends!
opening.visualSupports: Show and tell gestures, confident posture modeling, encouraging facial expressions

main.activity: Simple presentations: students choose 3-5 vocabulary cards to share. Can use gestures, pointing, or words. Partner sharing or small groups. Celebration of learning with applause and encouragement.
main.visualSupports: Model simple presentation format, use supportive gestures, provide visual choices

decisionPoints.question: What format best supports each student's comfort level?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Allow flexible presentation formats (individual, partner, group)
decisionPoints.ifNo: Use consistent format for all students

decisionPoints.question: Should presentations be individual, pairs, or small groups?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Use format that reduces anxiety and builds confidence
decisionPoints.ifNo: Try multiple formats to accommodate different comfort levels

closing.activity: Celebration circle: everyone shares one thing they learned and we celebrate with 'Bravo!' and applause.

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students too shy or overwhelmed to present
troubleshooting.then: Use puppet presentations, partner support, or simple pointing to vocabulary cards

lessons.realWorldConnection: Sharing ourselves with others builds community and confidence in language learning

lessons.title: Jeux et chansons françaises
lessons.oneGoal: Students will practice all vocabulary through games, songs, and playful activities (extension/enrichment)

opening.activity: Warm-up with favorite songs from previous lessons. Pierre puppet invites everyone to 'jouer' and 'chanter'!
opening.visualSupports: Playing gestures, singing actions, joyful expressions, rhythmic movements

main.activity: Learning station games: color sorting races, number hopscotch, animal charades, family matching, emotion faces game. French song circle with instruments.
main.visualSupports: Clear game demonstrations, encouraging gestures, celebratory movements

decisionPoints.question: Which games best reinforce learning without pressure?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Focus on successful, engaging games with multiple opportunities
decisionPoints.ifNo: Adjust game difficulty or provide more support

decisionPoints.question: Should we focus on group or individual activities?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Use format that promotes most engagement and success
decisionPoints.ifNo: Balance both group cooperation and individual achievement

closing.activity: Game appreciation circle: share favorite game and practice 'rire' together with joyful laughter.

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students too competitive or frustrated with games
troubleshooting.then: Emphasize fun over winning, provide multiple success opportunities, use cooperative games

lessons.realWorldConnection: Playing and having fun are universal ways children learn and connect

lessons.title: Histoires et images
lessons.oneGoal: Students will engage with simple French stories through pictures, gestures, and interactive storytelling (extension/enrichment)

opening.activity: Review games and laughter. Pierre puppet opens a special 'livre' and invites students to 'regarder' the pictures.
opening.visualSupports: Point to pictures clearly, use story gestures, create anticipation with expressions

main.activity: Interactive story time: simple French story with familiar vocabulary. Students help tell story through gestures and sounds. Create story pictures together. Story retelling with props.
main.visualSupports: Act out story elements, use predictable story patterns, encourage participation gestures

decisionPoints.question: Which story elements capture student attention?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Emphasize engaging elements and extend those parts
decisionPoints.ifNo: Adjust story pace or use more interactive elements

decisionPoints.question: Should we use big books, digital stories, or props?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Use format that best engages students and supports comprehension
decisionPoints.ifNo: Try multiple formats to maintain interest

closing.activity: Story appreciation: students share favorite 'image' from story and we create a class story memory.

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students losing attention during story or overwhelmed by new format
troubleshooting.then: Use shorter stories, more interactive elements, familiar vocabulary focus

lessons.realWorldConnection: Stories help us understand different perspectives and connect across cultures

lessons.title: Art et créativité française
lessons.oneGoal: Students will create visual art while using French vocabulary for colors, shapes, and creative expression (extension/enrichment)

opening.activity: Review story images. Pierre puppet becomes an artist and wants to 'dessiner' and 'créer' beautiful things.
opening.visualSupports: Drawing gestures, creating motions, appreciation expressions for 'beau'

main.activity: Art creation stations: draw with 'rouge, bleu, jaune', create family portraits, design animal pictures. Art sharing circle with vocabulary practice. Make it 'beau' together!
main.visualSupports: Demonstrate art techniques, use color vocabulary while creating, show appreciation gestures

decisionPoints.question: How do students best express creativity while using French?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Encourage natural integration of French into creative process
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on art creation with gentle French vocabulary integration

decisionPoints.question: Should we focus on process or product?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Emphasize creative process and French vocabulary use
decisionPoints.ifNo: Celebrate finished products and artistic expression

closing.activity: Art gallery walk: admire everyone's 'beau' creations and practice appreciation in French.

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students frustrated with art skills or materials
troubleshooting.then: Focus on effort and creativity, provide easier materials, emphasize personal expression

lessons.realWorldConnection: Art is a universal language that complements verbal communication

lessons.title: Cuisiner et goûter
lessons.oneGoal: Students will explore French food vocabulary through safe tasting, cooking activities, and cultural exploration (extension/enrichment)

opening.activity: Review art and beauty. Pierre puppet is hungry and wants to 'manger' something 'délicieux'!
opening.visualSupports: Eating gestures, delicious expressions, cooking motions, appreciation faces

main.activity: Safe food exploration: look at French foods, simple food preparation (mixing, arranging), taste testing with vocabulary. Cultural food discussion with pictures. Kitchen role-play.
main.visualSupports: Safe food handling demonstration, tasting expressions, cultural food appreciation

decisionPoints.question: How do we accommodate dietary restrictions and preferences?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Provide multiple options and respect all dietary needs
decisionPoints.ifNo: Use pictures and pretend food for inclusive experience

decisionPoints.question: Should we prepare food or use pictures and props?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Use safest approach that maximizes engagement and learning
decisionPoints.ifNo: Balance real and pretend food experiences

closing.activity: Food appreciation circle: share something 'délicieux' we discovered and practice gratitude in French.

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students with food anxieties or dietary restrictions feeling excluded
troubleshooting.then: Use inclusive alternatives, focus on cultural appreciation, emphasize choice and comfort

lessons.realWorldConnection: Food brings families and communities together across all cultures

lessons.title: Musique et mouvement
lessons.oneGoal: Students will explore French through music, rhythm, and coordinated movement activities (extension/enrichment)

opening.activity: Review delicious experiences. Pierre puppet hears 'musique' and wants everyone to 'bouger ensemble'!
opening.visualSupports: Musical conducting gestures, moving together motions, rhythm demonstration

main.activity: Musical exploration stations: instruments with French vocabulary, movement to French songs, rhythm games with counting, partner dancing. Create class song with familiar vocabulary.
main.visualSupports: Demonstrate musical movements, encourage creative expression, model group coordination

decisionPoints.question: How does music enhance or challenge student attention?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Use music strategically to support focus and engagement
decisionPoints.ifNo: Adjust volume, tempo, or complexity to match student needs

decisionPoints.question: Should we use recorded music or create our own sounds?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Use approach that most engages students and supports learning
decisionPoints.ifNo: Balance both recorded and created music experiences

closing.activity: Musical goodbye: create class rhythm with French vocabulary words and 'bouger ensemble' finale.

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students overwhelmed by noise or unable to coordinate movements
troubleshooting.then: Use quieter music, simpler movements, provide quiet participation options

lessons.realWorldConnection: Music and movement are joyful ways people celebrate and communicate in every culture

lessons.title: Notre célébration française
lessons.oneGoal: Students will celebrate their French learning journey through showcase activities, reflection, and community sharing (extension/enrichment)

opening.activity: Review musical joy. Pierre puppet announces it's time to 'célébrer' because everyone should feel 'fier' of their French learning!
opening.visualSupports: Celebration gestures, proud expressions, achievement recognition motions

main.activity: Learning celebration showcase: students choose favorite activities from 20 lessons to demonstrate. French learning portfolio sharing. Celebration activities with all vocabulary. Community appreciation circle.
main.visualSupports: Supportive celebration gestures, achievement recognition, community appreciation expressions

decisionPoints.question: How do we honor each student's unique learning journey?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Celebrate individual progress and different learning styles
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on group achievements and shared experiences

decisionPoints.question: Should celebration be classroom-focused or include families?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Include families if possible for broader community celebration
decisionPoints.ifNo: Keep celebration intimate and classroom-focused

closing.activity: Final celebration circle: each student shares one French word they love and we 'réussir' together with a big group hug!

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students sad about ending or feeling they didn't learn enough
troubleshooting.then: Focus on continuation, celebrate all growth, emphasize ongoing French journey

lessons.realWorldConnection: Celebrating learning achievements builds confidence and motivation for continued language exploration
